second_order: relocating and starting an AMD mark
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants moving from a lost Radeon mark to choosing a new place and beginning an AMD mark with a very small crew; what varies is locating, proposing, accepting, and beginning the build.

second_order: calling people to defend and repair AMD marks
theme_note: These calls treat AMD imagery as something people should actively protect or restore; the target and urgency vary.

second_order: finding and sharing where to help
theme_note: These codes orient people who do not yet know where the canvas effort is or how to reach it; one shares coordinates and one asks what is happening.

second_order: testing and policing April Fools hardware claims
theme_note: Participants collectively work out whether hardware news is a prank and how to respond; practices range from warning and sarcasm to teasing, rejecting clickbait, removal, and exasperation.

second_order: working out what the AMD mark should look like
theme_note: These codes negotiate the visible mark rather than merely defending its existence: colour, border, neighbouring overlap, and additional ATI imagery vary within the practice.

second_order: shifting help from AMD to another community
theme_note: This single code records a participant finishing their AMD contribution and moving effort to r/thenetherlands; it does not yet belong with a broader repeated practice.

second_order: putting hardware pranks into circulation
theme_note: These posts present invented or ambiguous hardware news for April 1; what varies is an obvious joke image versus title-only retirement claims whose status cannot be settled.

second_order: repairing an underspecified prank post
theme_note: The poster twice apologises for omitting the discussion text needed to frame the leak thread; both codes are the same small housekeeping practice.

second_order: arguing out whether oven-reflow works
theme_note: The possible troll recruits participants into practical disagreement about temperatures, capacitors, solder, BGA faults, evidence, and prior results; the practice is testing a repair claim even though the post seriousness remains unsettled.

second_order: arguing what April Fools posts should be allowed
theme_note: Participants debate whether false hardware news should be banned, labelled, deleted, tolerated as fun, or used as practice spotting fakes; later objections ask where joking becomes mistreating users.

second_order: turning a firmware prank into a board-stability dispute
theme_note: After the fake fix is exposed, participants exchange, defend, diagnose, and complain about the real Crosshair board; the shared practice is using the prank thread to argue the product actual state.

second_order: celebrating and mourning the mark together
theme_note: Participants turn the shared mark into an occasion for collective pride, admiration, survival claims, and later mourning; the moment ranges from we did it to it is over.

second_order: negotiating borders and peace with Polish neighbours
theme_note: These exchanges treat coexistence as practical bargaining over expansion help, non-invasion, a three-pixel border, truce terms, and suspected violations; cooperation and distrust vary inside the same practice.

second_order: contesting how much r/place talk belongs on the front page
theme_note: This first code asks the room to condense canvas posts rather than spam the subreddit; later slices can extend it if front-page volume becomes a repeated practice.

second_order: answering canvas threats with counterattack plans
theme_note: This single code proposes sabotage in return for reported sabotage; it is an outward counterattack plan rather than maintaining the AMD mark itself.

second_order: making jokes out of damaged pixels
theme_note: This single code laughs at the damaged AMD lettering as R7 Vegan; it is play made from a canvas defect rather than design work or an April Fools hardware prank.

second_order: calling off and disputing a witch hunt
theme_note: One post asks the room to stop pursuing someone after a fix, while its answer refuses to treat manipulation as a simple mistake; the shared practice is arguing over blame inside the repair effort.

second_order: adapting a script for the AMD logo
theme_note: These codes share participants offering an automation tool for the AMD mark, then asking for the tool to be altered; the joking attribution varies from the practical adaptation work.

second_order: making jokes out of the RYZENATI name
theme_note: Both codes turn the combined lettering into wordplay; Italian and Illuminati associations vary.

second_order: arriving late to the logo effort
theme_note: This single code is a participant apologizing for arriving after the coordinated work had begun and belongs with no other practice.

second_order: explaining and judging how r/place works
theme_note: These codes explain the canvas to confused or sceptical participants and judge what its competition produced; describing pixel mechanics, pointing to a timelapse, laughing, condemning wasted time, and defending cooperation vary.

second_order: arguing whether the logo effort was fanboy culture
theme_note: These codes dispute whether making and defending the corporate mark expressed community cooperation, competitive support, victimhood, or militant fanboy identity; condemnation, defence, explanation, and qualified affiliation vary.
